speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a pediatric patient presenting with a limp and localized pain, but no fever. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me exactly where the pain is located and what activity makes it worse?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful; a 7-year-old with a limp and left knee pain often points toward a hip issue referred to the knee. Did the pain start gradually or did you notice it suddenly? Also, does he have difficulty getting up from a sitting position or does the pain worsen when he lies down?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The pain is localized to your left knee and worsens with running or walking, but you have no fever. To differentiate between a hip pathology like Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease or slipped capital femoral epiphysis and a primary knee issue, I need to perform a physical exam. Can you lie on your back and let me move your left hip while you tell me if it hurts?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Pending physical exam results (Galeazzi sign, internal rotation of hip, and range of motion).
